Original context:
With the GNU C compiler, you may wish to use the ‘-MM’ flag instead
of ‘-M’.  This omits prerequisites on system header files.
See Options Controlling the Preprocessor in Using GNU CC, for details.

Publisher excerpt(s):
-MM ¶


--user-dependencies



Like -M but do not mention header files that are found in
system header directories, nor header files that are included,
directly or indirectly, from such a header.



This implies that the choice of angle brackets or double quotes in an
‘#include’ directive does not in itself determine whether that
header appears in -MM dependency output.
